explanation: The `<form>` element acts as an interactive container. `action` specifies the destination URL handler, and `method` specifies the HTTP transfer verb (`GET` or `POST`).

title: Diverse Input Types and Attributes
ques: Demonstrate the use of HTML5 input types: `text`, `email`, `password`, `number`, and `checkbox` paired with accessible `<label>` elements.
explanation: HTML5 input types automatically activate tailored virtual keyboards on mobile devices and provide built-in type validation before submission.

title: Button Types: Submit, Reset, and Button
ques: Explain the three values of the button `type` attribute: `submit`, `reset`, and `button`. Provide code samples for each.
explanation: The default button type in forms is `submit`. Setting `type="button"` prevents unintentional form submissions when triggering JavaScript client functions.

title: Native HTML5 Form Validation
ques: Demonstrate native HTML5 constraint validation using attributes: `required`, `pattern` (regular expression), `minlength`, `maxlength`, and custom error hints.

answer.content:
<form action="/submit" method="POST">
  <label for="zipCode">US Zip Code (5 digits):</label>
  <input 
    type="text" 
    id="zipCode" 
    name="zipCode" 
    required 
    pattern="[0-9]{5}" 
    title="Please enter exactly 5 numerical digits (e.g. 90210)" 
    minlength="5" 
    maxlength="5" 
  />
  <button type="submit">Verify Postal Code</button>
</form>

explanation: HTML5 constraint validation checks inputs before submitting, showing localized browser tooltips based on `pattern`, `minlength`, `maxlength`, and `title` without needing custom JavaScript.
